record.paper_title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
record.original_question: Instead of treating the epidemic threshold as a single critical value, can one formulate it in terms of the probability that an epidemic occurs under a specified set of conditions, such as when transmission and infection parameters are known or can be estimated with reasonable error? More broadly, can epidemic-threshold theory be reframed as a function of epidemic likelihood so that intervention costs and benefits can be evaluated more finely?

evidence.quote: A related problem of interest is to estimate the probability of an epidemic given a particular set of conditions.

The probability of epidemic is not typically estimated in conjunction with the epidemic threshold. Perhaps this could be accomplished by framing the epidemic threshold as a function of the likelihood of epidemic rather than as a singular value.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E(t)) be a temporal network on a finite vertex set V whose edge set E(t) varies with time t in a specified family of contact processes (e.g. activity-driven, switching, or empirically measured contact sequences). On G run a stochastic SIS or SIR epidemic process with per-contact transmission rate β and recovery rate μ, starting from a small set of initially infected vertices. Define an "epidemic" to be the event that the cumulative or prevalence trajectory exceeds a fixed threshold (e.g. that the fraction of ever-infected vertices exceeds some ε > 0 before extinction, or that the prevalence persists above ε for a time exceeding T).

Classically, an epidemic threshold is defined as a critical value of a control parameter λ = β/μ (or of a spectral quantity of the temporal contact structure) above which an epidemic occurs with positive probability in the large-network limit and below which it almost surely dies out.

Reformulate this notion probabilistically:

(a) Given the temporal network model G and parameters (β, μ) — possibly known only up to specified estimation errors with a prior or confidence region — develop a quantitative theory expressing the probability P_epi(β, μ, G) that an epidemic (in the above sense) occurs, as an explicit or computable function of the model parameters and of the temporal-network statistics.

(b) Replace the singular critical value by a level set {(β, μ) : P_epi(β, μ, G) = p} for p ∈ (0, 1), and characterize the geometry, scaling, and dependence on temporal-network features (degree distribution, inter-event time distribution, temporal correlations, spectral radius of suitable supra-adjacency operators) of these level sets.

(c) Using the resulting likelihood-based threshold, formulate and solve an intervention-optimization problem: given a cost functional C(I) for an intervention I that modifies (β, μ, G), and a benefit functional B measuring the reduction of P_epi achieved by I, determine intervention strategies minimizing C subject to constraints on P_epi or maximizing B − C.

Provide rigorous results — exact formulas, asymptotic expansions, or provable bounds — for at least one nontrivial family of temporal-network models, and prove that the level-set formulation reduces to the classical epidemic threshold in an appropriate limit (e.g. as p → 0 with the network size tending to infinity).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction in the temporal-networks epidemic-threshold literature. While probabilistic outbreak-size analyses exist for specific models (branching-process approximations, percolation on contact networks), a unified reframing of the epidemic threshold as a level set of the epidemic probability — integrated with parameter-uncertainty and intervention cost-benefit analysis on general temporal networks — does not appear to have been established. No definitive resolution was identified.

status_evidence.title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Review identifies probability-of-epidemic formulations of thresholds as an open research problem.
status_evidence.claim: The reformulation of epidemic thresholds via the probability of an epidemic is listed as an open question in the temporal-networks review.
